title: Inference management
summary: The Inference area manages vLLM and llama.cpp from the controller. Open /inference from desktop or mobile navigation, or from the surface directory. It uses your existing sign-in.
html:
Inference management

The Inference area manages vLLM and llama.cpp from the controller. Open /inference from desktop or mobile navigation, or from the surface directory. It uses your existing sign-in, appearance settings and agent permission policies. Model engines, builds and installations run in supervised processes and separate environments; the controller remains available while you manage them.

Maintainers can trace the shared implementation in inference architecture and worker ownership.

Embeddings for Knowledge and Memory

Choose New Embeddings instance, then open Configuration → Downloads. The balanced Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B Q8_0 preset is preselected. BGE, Qwen 4B and Qwen 8B are also available. Opening this section only displays information. Install & start prepares dependencies, downloads pinned model files, verifies them, starts the instance, and tests its embedding output. Progress survives a browser or controller restart. Jobs & Logs lists the installation immediately, including runtime dependency downloads before the model download starts. Both views show stages and measured download progress; cancellation and retry are available.

After the instance is ready, enable Use as Embeddings. Verification automatically updates the Knowledge provider, text model, dimensions, and endpoint in every workspace, and queues any required index rebuild for Documents and Memory. Workspaces created or opened later inherit the same selection. No additional manual settings change is needed. Existing BGE indexes and accepted tasks retain their captured encoder. A model change builds replacement document generations before activation. Memory exact values remain in its authoritative store and lexical search remains available during rebuilding.

Selecting Use as Embeddings applies a managed worker to both Documents and Memory, including workers on another managed host. Manually configured external embedding connections still require enabling Memory's explicit remote-processing option. External text embeddings do not move images, reranking, or extraction to that endpoint. Embeddings have no chat temperature, output-token settings, or fallback to Main. Internally managed embedding workers do not receive generated API keys. Restarting an older worker removes its automatically generated key requirement.

An administrator can choose Auto or CPU, eligible NVIDIA GPU UUIDs, headroom, memory budget, batches and idle release in Knowledge's installation settings. The separate CUDA environment must pass real inference checks before bundled workers use it. The panel reports requested and actual execution and fallback reasons. Existing Main, Helper and Vision allocations are preserved. Insufficient resources or incompatible drivers retain CPU operation.

Configuration → Encoder specification also supports custom llama.cpp and vLLM pooling instances using registered models and inspected runtimes. External embedding endpoints can be configured in Model routing. Encoder identity is immutable after configuration; create another instance to change the encoder. Curated presets need no manual model paths or launch arguments.

See embedding qualification and measurements for tested configurations and the remaining platform qualification gates.

Chat toolbar serving indicator

The chip icon beside the SQL-save button controls one instance: the main managed model, or, when none is assigned, the last successfully loaded local instance. Mobile shows the same icon in its header. Helper connections do not affect it. The last loaded instance is remembered across stops and controller restarts, including instances loaded before this feature was installed. The icon is hidden only when neither a main managed model nor a previously loaded local instance exists.

Appearance Meaning
Red The instance is not serving: stopped, starting, recovering or stopping.
Green The instance is warmed up, idle and ready to serve.
Flashing green The instance is ready and requests are in flight.
Gray Current status is unavailable; this does not mean idle.

The tooltip identifies the instance and whether it is the main model or the last loaded instance. Reduced-motion mode uses static colors with the same accessible descriptions.

Click a stopped instance's red icon to start it using its last successfully served configuration. Newer saved edits are preserved. If management is stopped, its existing Start operation runs first. Missing previous configurations and lifecycle conflicts direct you to Inference. Other states open Inference without starting anything. Status refreshes never start models or enable GPU monitoring. Fresh status checks keep the indicator current even if live updates disconnect. If those checks fail or become stale, the indicator turns gray until status is known.

Which installation includes inference?

Linux source installations include inference management automatically:

./install.sh --launch

Run this from the project folder. --launch starts the controller after setup. To install without starting it, use ./install.sh, then ./startup.sh when ready. There is no inference enable flag on install.sh. Installation prepares management dependencies; you still choose your runtime, model and launch settings.

For compiled Linux x86_64 controllers, the build selects the feature:

Build option Result
--inference=both Both controller artifacts; the default for Linux server builds.
--inference=enabled smto-server-inference, including managed inference and external connections.
--inference=disabled smto-server-external, using externally configured model endpoints.

From the repository root, for example:

./build/build --component server --inference=both

These are options for the compiled builder, not the installer or startup command. The feature is immutable in a compiled artifact. An external-only binary has no inference management UI, API, tools, workers or state; a runtime setting cannot add them. Existing external endpoint and controller prompt-caching settings remain available. Gateway builds are unchanged. Non-Linux controllers and packages from the older builders use external endpoints.

Find the controls

Use the magnifying glass or Ctrl+F / ⌘F to open the shared search popup. It filters workflow navigation and highlights matching text on the current page. Escape closes search and restores all tabs. Tab links can be bookmarked, for example /inference#models or /inference#runtimes.

Tab What you can do
Overview Check health, resources, recent operations and agent/helper connections.
Hosts & GPUs Manage local/remote hosts, watch live NVIDIA-SMI output, inspect hardware and reservations, and review placement.
Storage & Preferences Set storage paths, scanning/log retention and credentials; start, restart or shut down inference management.
Environments & Builds Register and inspect existing environments/binaries, install managed vLLM, build llama.cpp and remove runtimes.
Models Configure roots, scan files, inspect metadata/context, and select or download Hugging Face repository revisions and files.
Caching Inspect engine cache configuration/evidence and edit controller prompt-caching settings.
Jobs & Logs Follow installations, builds, downloads and diagnostics; cancel, retry where supported, and export logs.
Instances Find instances across both backends, open details, configure, validate, start and stop.

The sidebar groups setup before operation, with Instances last. Storage & Preferences keeps its existing #preferences bookmark.

Each Hosts & GPUs section can be collapsed independently. Monitoring panels start collapsed; open them to view live readings. Collapsing a panel pauses its display updates, while an explicitly started timeline capture continues.

Hosts & GPUs → GPU power limits lists NVIDIA GPUs in a compact table on the selected Power host, with current limits, saved targets and status. Expand a GPU row to see its slider, supported range, default limit and UUID. Drag to choose watts, then select Apply. Collapsing a row preserves unapplied slider edits. A saved target does not mean the change succeeded. Limits affect all work on that physical GPU, including already-running instances.

If the host requires sudo, expand Sudo password and save the password for the OS account running its portal. Update password replaces it and retries saved limits. Passwords are kept in that host's private server-side secrets store and are never returned to the browser. Remote hosts need the updated standalone portal. Each host remembers targets by GPU UUID and attempts restoration in the background when its portal starts. Failed restoration shows a warning; it never prevents the controller or inference instances from starting. Use Apply to retry.

This feature uses only nvidia-smi; missing drivers/tools and unsupported devices show an error. Existing installed portals need a service update/reinstall to remove NoNewPrivileges=true so sudo can run. Custom service definitions must also permit elevation, and the portal's OS account must be allowed to use sudo. The portal still runs as its normal user; no extra service or GPU driver is installed.

Hosts & GPUs → Live NVIDIA-SMI shows the selected host’s GPU utilization, memory, temperature, power and process table. It refreshes every two seconds while the pane is open and the browser tab is visible. Use Pause to inspect a sample, Refresh output for a single update, or the copy icon to copy the table. The most recent sample replaces the previous one; it is not saved as a log. Remote hosts need an updated standalone portal with live GPU output support. Missing NVIDIA-SMI, driver errors and connection failures appear in the pane. This read-only view does not launch inference or change GPU settings.

Server resources, directly below NVIDIA-SMI, has llama.cpp and vLLM tabs for the same Trace host. Each shows the combined system RAM and CPU used by that host’s portal-managed servers and workers, including RPC and Ray workers. CPU is normalized to the entire host: 100% means all logical CPUs are busy. RAM uses proportional resident memory (PSS) to apportion shared pages; when those counters are unavailable, an explicitly labelled RSS estimate can count shared memory more than once. Incomplete readings are marked unavailable rather than zero.

The two graphs retain up to ten minutes of samples in this browser page and clear on reload. Both backends update every two seconds while the pane is open and visible. Pause resource monitoring and Refresh resources operate independently of NVIDIA-SMI. Use the arrow keys on a graph to inspect samples. Collection gaps remain visible, and CPU shows Collecting… while establishing its first baseline. This monitor also works on hosts without NVIDIA hardware. Remote hosts need a portal version supporting the server-resources operation.

Requests & GPU timeline adds a correlated view below Server resources. Choose a Host, then Start monitoring. The selected GPU's utilization and fan setting use the percentage axis; temperature uses the °C axis. Shaded intervals show SMTO model HTTP attempts, including retries and cancelled or failed attempts. The capture can also include marked routing preflight failures that sent no HTTP request; those carry no usage. Dense traffic is grouped visually. Choose an instance and a 1, 5 (default), or 10 minute window to narrow the view.

Hover over the graph or use its arrow keys to inspect readings at the same time. Select up to two requests to compare input/output tokens, reported cached tokens, time to first output, provider prompt-processing time, and request duration. Unsupported or missing measurements remain Unknown. Non-streaming responses do not expose a first-output timestamp. Backend totals under the chart include direct clients and overlap the SMTO requests; they are not additional calls. Those counters retain their backend sampling interval and reset on a new launch.

GPU readings are device-wide, including unrelated workloads, and one-second sampling can miss shorter spikes. Fan setting is the percentage reported by NVIDIA, not measured RPM; some devices do not report it and some report more than 100%. Remote readings carry an alignment uncertainty. Cached-token reports provide evidence of prefix reuse; a quiet GPU or shorter request alone does not establish a cache hit. Prompt-processing time and time to first output are different measurements.

Monitoring continues while you navigate to Chat or Settings, with a shared indicator and Stop monitoring button. Pause chart freezes inspection without stopping collection; Jump to live catches up. Hidden views stop rendering and fetching chart records. Changing hosts starts a fresh capture. Export JSON/CSV exports the retained capture, including numerical usage and timings but no prompt or response content. A live capture can change during export; the export includes change and gap indicators. Stop monitoring first to freeze the retained observations for export.

Captures are held in controller memory: the most recent ten minutes, at most 600 samples per GPU, 5,000 request records, and 8 MiB per session. Eviction and collection gaps are explicit. A connected page renews the session every 15 seconds; collection expires after 120 seconds without renewal. Stopped captures remain exportable for ten minutes. Controller restart ends these sessions. Older remote portals show an upgrade message while available request observations continue. Monitoring does not generate model requests or change cache settings.

Instances opens a compact list with search and status, backend and host filters. Open an instance for Overview, Configuration, Logs and Diagnostics. Returning to the list keeps its filters and scroll position. Expand a list row to find Duplicate and Delete profile. In instance details, these actions are in the More menu.

Configuration groups Basics, GPU & Context, Performance & Cache, and collapsed Advanced controls. Runtime inspection supplies the option catalog. Advanced controls preserve explicit options, imported aliases, environment variables, raw argument ordering and custom templates. JSON edits are validated before saving or leaving the editor. Save/Discard appears for configuration edits; saving never restarts a process. Switching detail tabs retains the draft; leaving a dirty instance asks whether to save, discard, or cancel. Diagnostics contains cache and cancellation experiments; cancellation route configuration is under Basics.

For llama.cpp instances, Configuration → Basics → Detect repeat discourages repeated text. It starts off for new instances, with History length (tokens) set to 64. Turning it on uses a repetition penalty of 1.1 over that window; turning it off sets the penalty to 1.0 and retains the length. Save the profile, then use Apply / Restart to apply the change. Saving alone does not restart it. This is a generation setting, not a detector that stops repeated tool calls. Existing custom values are preserved until edited. Raw arguments, environment overrides and special history values remain editable in Advanced. If the selected runtime does not advertise both options, the simple controls are unavailable; use Refresh runtime options in Advanced to refresh its capabilities.

First setup

  1. In Hosts & GPUs, choose the local host or register a remote portal host.
  2. In Storage & Preferences, choose storage locations, model roots and credentials.
  3. In Environments & Builds, register and inspect an existing environment or llama-server binary, or create a managed runtime.
  4. In Models, scan existing files or select a Hugging Face repository, revision and files to download. Select every required GGUF shard and any needed projector. Gated repositories require your authorized token.
  5. In Instances, choose New instance. The four steps cover backend/host, runtime/model, GPU/context, and review/validation. Networking and advanced controls are optional disclosures. Links to missing prerequisites retain the draft during this session; return to Instances and choose Resume setup.
  6. In GPU & Context, select eligible devices. Always use recommended model weight split defaults on for new and existing instances. It calculates and validates a split at every start, restart, and recovery. Pipeline mode may use fewer GPUs when the model fits. Manual split values are preserved while their controls are disabled. Switch it off to edit TP/PP, layer allocation, and GPU weight proportions, or to apply Recommend split once. GPU selection, context, headroom, split mode, and GPU offload settings stay editable. Changes apply on the next launch. With at least two GPUs, choose Pipeline Parallelism (current behavior) or Tensor Parallelism. Tensor uses every selected GPU on the serving host: vLLM uses equal tensor shards with one pipeline stage; llama.cpp offers recommended or manual tensor proportions. Its diagram shows GPUs sharing layers. Tensor's context, offload depth, proportions, and cache formats are saved separately, so switching back restores Pipeline settings. llama.cpp Tensor is experimental, requires Flash Attention and non-quantized KV cache, and disables native auto-fit. Incompatible advanced Pipeline values remain saved but inactive in Tensor. With one GPU the selector is disabled and single-GPU execution applies; the Tensor preference is remembered when a second GPU is selected. Explicit Tensor currently requires one host. The preview always shows the actual resolved mode.
  7. Choose Create profile, or Create & start. With automatic splitting on, Create & start validates automatically; errors block launch. The preview and Validate controls remain available. With automatic splitting off, validate first. A saved profile can be started later from its list row or Overview. Follow loading in Logs and confirm readiness.
  8. In Overview → Agent & helper connections, choose the ready instance and served model, then Use this connection. You do not need to copy its URL. Each button saves its own role; changes in the other form remain unsaved until you use that form's button. Changing the instance clears the previous model name.

For compatible llama.cpp runtimes, GPU & Context → Auto-fit context to GPU memory lets llama.cpp choose context size at startup. It defaults off. Enabling it disables the saved context controls without discarding their values; turning it off restores them. Your K/V cache formats and GPU placement remain configured. Advanced fitting options exposes the runtime's minimum context and GPU memory margin when supported. The fitting margin is separate from headroom used for planning estimates. Save the profile, then explicitly start or restart to apply changes. Context capacity and KV estimates remain unknown until the runtime provides evidence of the chosen size.

Model downloads open Jobs & Logs, where each download shows a live progress bar, percentage, downloaded/total size, current file and completed file count. Progress includes resumed transfers and validated cached files across the selected model's shards. Unknown totals use an indeterminate bar. Finalizing download means the files have downloaded and the library is updating; Download complete confirms both are finished. Failed or cancelled jobs retain their last reported progress. Remote downloads report progress from the selected host's updated portal.

Assign agent roles

Each regular instance’s Overview has Use as Main, Use as Helper, Use as Vision, and Use as Embeddings switches. The three chat roles save immediately for new tasks, including while the instance is stopped. The same instance may hold all three roles. Assigning a role already held by another instance reports an error naming that instance; clear it first or replace the assignment in Settings → Model Routing.

Inference and Settings share one configuration: the last successful save wins. Settings overrides update the instance switches, and changing an unassigned instance’s profile does not reclaim a role. Managed assignments follow the instance’s current endpoint and served model after Apply / Restart. Accepted tasks retain their captured routing and generation settings.

Turning Main off leaves no Main configured and blocks new tasks until one is selected. Clearing Helper uses each route’s existing fallback policy. Clearing Vision falls back to Main, which must support image input for image requests.

Use as Embeddings checks the selected model's declared embedding configuration, prepares a separate worker on the same serving host, and verifies actual vectors before replacing the current embeddings assignment. Chat roles and processes keep running. Existing verified model files are reused; missing pinned model artifacts or an isolated compatible runtime download only after activation. Unsupported or ambiguous models show an explanation and Choose an embedding preset.

The verified encoder is applied to Documents and Memory in every workspace automatically. Document indexes rebuild in the background while existing generations remain searchable. Memory semantic matching is enabled and backfilled; its separate automatic-use preference is retained. Both lanes use the selected managed host without a second Memory activation step.

GPU execution is observed from runtime offload information or GPU memory belonging to the worker process. Missing optional logs do not stop an encoder whose embedding requests passed verification: its device is shown as unknown when evidence is unavailable. A runtime that explicitly reports zero GPU layers still fails a requested GPU launch.

Progress distinguishes encoder readiness from index rebuilding. Retry and cancel survive page reloads. Turning off the switch cancels preparation or restores the previous assignment and settings where this activation still owns them; later settings edits, downloaded files and existing indexes are retained. Source model changes require Use updated model to change the frozen embedding worker. Older remote hosts must be updated to support automatic embedding preparation.

Configure vision

Open Configuration → Vision and enable vision. With llama.cpp, Automatic selects an unambiguous projector associated with the text model’s pinned repository revision and downloads it on the serving host when you save. Existing matching projectors are reused. Missing provenance or multiple candidates requires a manual projector selection. The text model’s quantization stays unchanged: Q6 text weights can use a separate BF16 projector.

The section shows download progress, retry/cancel controls, and the running instance’s verified image support. A ready projector or enabled setting is not proof of working image input. Save, then Apply / Restart to load the encoder. vLLM uses its native multimodal controls instead of a separate GGUF projector; the installed runtime must advertise the required controls.

Enabling Use as Vision also enables and saves vision configuration and starts projector preparation. It does not restart the instance. Saving vision as disabled clears that instance’s Vision role. Existing raw vision arguments remain unchanged until you explicitly configure this section; remove conflicting advanced arguments when moving their values into the managed Vision controls.

Change a running instance

Saved configuration, the running launch snapshot and observed evidence describe different things. Editing a profile does not change its process.

  1. Edit the profile and choose Save profile.
  2. Choose Validate, then Review changes to inspect the saved-versus-running difference, active requests and affected tasks.
  3. Choose Apply / Restart and confirm the change.
  4. Follow the operation in Overview and the instance logs.

The controller blocks new requests to the affected endpoint and queues a background checkpoint. Launch proceeds without waiting for the checkpoint or active requests to finish. Active requests are interrupted when workers stop. It verifies readiness and model compatibility, refreshes bindings and invalidates stale capability/cache/continuation evidence, then releases the operation's admission hold. Waiting requests can recheck admission; this does not restart a cancelled task or guarantee recovery of an interrupted request.

If the candidate fails, the controller attempts restoration of the previous successful launch snapshot. The failed saved candidate and logs remain available for correction. Failed restoration retains the endpoint hold while management remains available. Stop takes precedence over a pending restart, and cancelled tasks stay cancelled. Stop also works with invalid unsaved form edits.

Force Stop, next to Stop, immediately kills the selected instance's owned worker processes, including worker descendants on its participating hosts. It skips the graceful process shutdown period, and can escalate a Stop that is already waiting. Active model requests are interrupted. Unsaved profile edits are not applied. Cleanup verifies process exit before releasing reservations; a failed or unreachable host remains reported as a cleanup failure. The instance stays stopped until explicitly started again.

Once Stop or Force Stop finishes successfully, its model-capacity hold is released. Deleting a task or conversation also cancels its model requests and releases their capacity immediately; this does not wait for background history cleanup. Controller restart discards old request reservations and inference holds without an unfinished lifecycle operation. A failed worker cleanup remains visible in the operation's logs.

Concurrent manual and agent edits use revisions; a conflict requires refreshing the saved state before applying another change. Duplicate lifecycle requests can use the same idempotency key without starting another operation.

Read instance and job output

Logs opens with up to 200 recent records and follows live output. Scroll upward or choose Pause tail to read without automatic scrolling; Jump to latest resumes following. Load older explicitly retrieves retained history, including previous participating hosts. Search, copy and export operate on loaded output. Export preserves structured JSONL records, including host/worker labels.

The viewer buffers at most 5,000 records or 4 MiB and mounts only visible rows. Large messages are shortened for display and marked; full retained local logs remain available through the download link. Remote hosts retain their own full logs. Leaving the view or hiding the browser tab stops its stream/polling; return resumes from the last cursor and reports any retention gap.

Archive reads scan backwards, at most 2 MiB per page. A sparse instance can have no matches in the recent window while older history remains available. Host errors appear beside the viewer and do not delay other hosts. Remote portals need bounded-log pagination support; older versions display an upgrade message. Job output uses the same bounded reader and viewer.

Build a runtime

In Environments & Builds, select the host and managed llama.cpp build workflow. Choose the source release or commit, installed/custom/managed CUDA toolkit, GPU architecture and build preset. Opening the page only inspects local settings and toolkits; it never contacts GitHub or NVIDIA's release catalog. Use Check now for releases to fetch available versions. Download & build validates the selected source and toolkit before starting compilation.

The CUDA toolkit defaults to Automatic — latest supported CUDA for custom builds. It selects the newest published NVIDIA toolkit compatible with the host's driver and GPU architectures that provides the required packages for its platform. Starting the build resolves the selected version and pins it for retries. Specific managed versions and installed toolkits remain selectable, and named build presets retain their pinned CUDA versions. Package resolution uses the CUDA capability reported by the NVIDIA driver, so an older system toolkit does not prevent building a newer supported runtime.

Jobs & Logs preserves stage progress and output through download, configuration, compilation and verification. A successful build registers the runtime; select it in a profile and validate before launch. Cancellation and supported retries use the existing job controls. Runtime removal provides a preview before removal.

Investigate caching

In Caching, choose an instance to compare requested engine settings, its running snapshot, finite RAM reservations and observed cache evidence. Unknown or unsupported evidence is not a cache hit. Controls shown in multiple views edit the same backend values; save and explicitly restart to apply them.

For llama.cpp, RAM prompt-cache budget offers Backend default, Off, 8/16/24/32 GiB, or a custom integer MiB value. A positive budget enables prompt reuse; Retain idle contexts controls whether idle contexts are saved into that cache. The preview shows the actual cache launch arguments, including --cache-ram N. GPU KV offloading is separate and stays unchanged. Check memory fit before using Apply / Restart. Saving only updates the profile; the running budget remains visible until a new launch uses the saved arguments.

Recent model calls shows the latest 64 controller observations in a sortable, filterable table. Expand a row for retries and configuration details. Unknown telemetry is shown as an em dash, not zero. Auto-refresh is pausable, and retained history clears on controller restart.

The controller prompt-caching editor is shared with Settings → Prompt caching. Its switches default off and affect request construction and controller reuse. Turning Prompt caching on here also enables the advertised --cache-prompt (llama.cpp) or --enable-prefix-caching (vLLM) option in the saved profiles connected to the agent or helpers. Connecting an instance while caching is on prepares its flag too. Unsupported or offline runtimes are reported for correction. Other profiles, external endpoints and cache RAM budgets stay unchanged. Running instances require Apply / Restart; the toggle does not restart them. Turning it off preserves backend options, which remain editable in each instance. The Settings entry point shares the controller policy and keeps engine setup manual.

Reading status, opening a page or refreshing evidence does not submit inference. Explicit diagnostics and comparisons can submit bounded test requests; use their progress and cancellation controls. This integration does not add native cache eviction, slot snapshots, or cache save/restore operations.

State, shutdown and remote hosts

Fresh management state lives in inference/ beside the controller's current-run database, normally beneath AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR (default artifacts for source launches). The inference database, private secrets, jobs and rotating logs remain the authoritative stores. Model roots, permanent installations and build-work locations are configurable separately.

An existing standalone portal is not discovered, imported, adopted or removed. A fresh controller state directory starts without its profiles or bindings. There are no automatic model downloads or background tuning. The standalone portal remains available for independent and remote hosts; its worker protocol continues to handle leases, reservations, remote builds/downloads, Ray and RPC.

Preferences → Restart inference restarts management and restores requested running profiles while keeping the controller UI available. Shutdown inference stops its workers and jobs; use Start inference to start management again. An intentional instance shutdown stays stopped. Controller shutdown also cleans up owned workers and jobs; cleanup failures retain ownership for retry. Controller startup recovers accepted operations and requested running profiles.

Agent and API access

The authenticated API is /api/agent/inference/v1. The inference.* tools use the same validated operations as the UI and follow existing capability and permission rules. Long operations return identifiers for status, result, errors, and cancellation or retry where supported. The controller persists an accepted agent tool result before interrupting the model serving that task.

The parity ledger maps every management contract to UI and tool access and records validation limits. Local llama.cpp hardware checks are recorded there; vLLM hardware was skipped, and remote Ray/RPC hardware parity has not been established.
